chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: The Wilton Crawley date where Morton and Russell's men clashed
summary: Morton arrived with his own group for a Wilton Crawley record date, and he and Crawley traded barbs until the players split the sides.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Now, you recorded with him at one time.
Yeah. Well, I recorded with... He was on the same record I was on with Wilton Crawley(?). Boy, that was somethin'.

I don't know how to even start that, because I don't know what happened. Russell was supposed to get a group to record with Wilton Crawley, and Jelly Roll was supposed to play piano. And Jelly Roll walked in there with his group. And there was a big conflict right there, because Wilton Crawley wanted Russell's group and Jelly was going to have his group -- he got his band with him. So I don't know, we compromised. Some of the guys played some of the records and the rest of them played on the other ones --
the rest of the record. Split it up, one of them things.
Because I remember once you told me it was like two prima donnas walking in, and...

Oh yeah, yeah! It was somethin' else. And they was at one another's throats all day long, making cracks at one another, you know. Yeah, Wilton Crawley had just finished playing the Lafayette Theatre, a Black theatre, and he had just finished playing a week there. So Jelly Roll is sittin' at the piano, makes a smart remark. He says, 'Well...'
...Wilton Crawley, and Jelly looks up from the piano.
"I dug you at the Lafayette Theatre" -- the Lafayette Theatre was in Harlem. So Wilton looks back at him and says, "Well, now you can dig me next week at the Paramount Theatre" -- downtown.
Oh, I see! Anyway, as I understand it, they squared off, because Jelly thought that the records would sell because he was on them.
Well, Jelly heard a little part on the
piano. He had a little break in the number. And Jelly said, 'This is gonna sell the number.' BRR-RUMMPH. Wilton said, 'Wilton Crawley's name is on the record. That's what's gonna sell the number.'
So anyway, you got through the day.
